category_title: Young children with persistent challenging behaviors and communication delays
student_description: Kayden is a 3-year-old with communication delays who uses challenging behaviors (screaming, hitting, throwing toys) to escape tasks like cleanup or to gain adult attention and desired items. He uniquely requires highly predictable routines, visual supports, and proactive contingencies (like First-Then statements), as reactive strategies—such as reprimands or redirection—inadvertently reinforce his challenging behaviors.

criteria.rationale: Kayden's communication delays mean he needs concrete, non-verbal ways to understand the sequence of expectations.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates visual schedules or visual supports to explicitly map out the steps of challenging routines.

criteria.rationale: By fulfilling Kayden's need for attention before a demand is placed, he is less likely to use screaming or hitting to get it later.
criteria.check: The long-term plan schedules dedicated time for positive, mutually enjoyable adult interaction immediately preceding known behavioral triggers.

criteria.rationale: Kayden struggles with unexpected transitions, so standardizing when they happen reduces his anxiety and resistance.
criteria.check: The long-term plan establishes a fixed, predictable pattern or schedule for when challenging routines (such as running errands) will occur.
